title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 4: foresight of sanctity not denied — but not proved as cause
pass_a_gloss: It is not to be denied that God foreknows the sanctity of those whom he elected unto glory: for it is impossible that God should not foreknow those things which he himself is about to do; and he himself works all our good things in us. But it is not enough for winning this cause, that it be proved God foresees good works, or the sanctity of the elect, unless besides it be shown that from this antecedent foresight God proceeds to electing. But this they can never wring out of the Apostle's words.
pass_b_english: Reply: of course God foreknows the holiness of those he elects to glory — he cannot fail to foreknow what he himself will do, and he works all our good in us. But proving that he foresees the elect's good works is not enough for their cause, unless they also show he elects from that prior foresight. And that they can never force out of Paul's words.
source_text: Non est negandum Deum praescire illorum sanctitatem quos elegit ad gloriam: impossibile enim est ut Deus non praesciat ea quae ipse facturus est; ipse autem omnia nostra bona in nobis operatur. Sed non satis est ad causam hanc obtinendam, ut probetur Deum praevidere bona opera, aut sanctitatem electorum, nisi insuper ostendatur ex hac praevisione antecedente Deum procedere ad eligendum. At hoc nunquam extorquere possunt ex verbis Apostoli.
